messages:
maya: Quick q — should console block saves when YAML drifts from runtime schema? I hit a case where editor accepted old header matcher syntax and runtime fails at deploy.

liam: Saw that. We made reads tolerant but writes currently allow the legacy shape. My vote: preflight lint should error on save for things that will break runtime. Block + clear message.

serena: How noisy would that be? Some orgs have a lot of legacy routes. Blocking saves could create support churn. Can we do severity levels: warn vs hard error?

aj: We should classify issues: schema-incompat, runtime-break, semantics-change. A drift-detector can tag each finding. Only `runtime-break` should block by default.

katie: UX note — if it's going to block, show a migration autofix inline. E.g. suggest replacing `headers:` -> `headerMatchers:` and show the diff before applying. Otherwise we'll get a flurry of support tickets.

maya: Agreed. Also we need telemetry: emit `route_save.preflight.breaks_runtime` (count + org tier + rule id) so we can prioritize migrations.

liam: Implementation idea: route-authoring service runs preflight pipeline: schema-validate -> drift-detector -> runtime-sim. We have the schema tests, but need a small runtime mock to detect fields that cause runtime errors.

aj: We can reuse the existing `route-fuzz` harness and add targeted examples as fixtures. Add integration tests that run the console preflight flow in CI.

ci-bot: preflight-lint: failed for draft/route-templates/legacy-header.yaml
logs: `RuntimeError: unknown field 'headers' at /spec/matchers`

serena: Practical: add a top-level annotation `x-console-suppressions` that teams can set to allow save-with-exceptions. Persist suppression in audit log and require an admin confirmation.

katie: Console UX: show a single-line banner with "Save anyway (recorded in audit)" plus a "Run migration" button. Make the migration preview editable.

liam: Edgecases: if we block saves we must handle rollouts and rollbacks. Add a feature flag `authoring.preflight_enforce_runtime_breaks` (default on for new orgs, opt-in for legacy). Also expose a team-level policy for auto-migration.

maya: Plan: PR will include schema version bump + new linter rule + migration autofix + telemetry + CI fixtures + console banner. I'll draft the route-authoring + console PR and assign code review.

aj: :thumbsup: Add the failing YAML to fixtures and a tiny runtime-mock test. If we track counts in telemetry we can measure impact before forcing migration.

maya: Example failing snippet to add to fixtures:
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Route
spec:
  matchers:
    - path: /users/*
      headers:  # legacy field — runtime rejects this
        - name: x-user
          value: ".*"
```

aj: Telemetry example: `emit_event("route_save.preflight", {"result":"breaks_runtime","rule":"headers_field","org_tier":"pro"})`

maya: Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/route-authoring/pull/789 (WIP) — assigning @liam and @serena to review.

ci-bot: ci: preflight-unit-tests passed (45s); integration-preflight pending.
